data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's failure mode is indistinguishable from the subject's failure mode under the same installation, and the 3-of-26 result is the number of cases where the test's own failure was counted as the subject's mutation loss.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test harness's operational failures are logged separately from mutation losses, then the conflation cannot occur.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation loss was due to a genuine code-level mutation that was not caught, rather than a harness failure, then the mechanism is wrong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If re-running the test with a different harness (but the same shown-to-fail-first installation) recovers the 1/9 mutation, then the harness was the cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under shown-to-fail-first installation, the test harness's own failure modes (e.g., timeouts, resource exhaustion, or guard installation errors) were recorded as if they were the subject's mutation losses. The 1/9 mutation lost under compile.py was a case where the test harness failed to run the mutation at all, but this was recorded as the mutation being 'lost.' The test constrained the subject by conflating its own operational failures with the subject's behavioral properties. The 3-of-26 distribution reflects the number of cases where the test's operational failure was misattributed to the subject.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
